Montréal Communiqué 


2 For release at will 


June 9, 1970 


"If you want it, move it," urges the editor in the latest 
issue of Y Action, the newly re-vamped national publication 
of the YMCAs of Canada. 

"Moving it means taking action. More specifically, it 
means action which necessitates a change in some attitudes,” 
explains 2l-year old Jim Wolfe. 

He insists that if people really want something, they 
won't simply talk about wanting it. They will move and act 
on it, despite attitudinal obstacles. 

Noting that dissatisfaction with institutions is growing-- 
and not only amongst young people--he says action by private 
citizens and groups of people is “effervescing"” and filling 
the gap. 

"The challenge...is to encourage this effervescence, 
respond to it, and then act...That may mean a lot of flak, 
and institutions which are relevant to where people are at 
will be able to handle it.” 

In line with a near-unamimous decision at the recent 
annual meeting of the Canadian YMCAs, Y Action is now “a 
publication for the expression of opinions of youth in 
Canada, published by youth, with editorial authority in 
the hands of youth".
